title: a correctly installed shim carrier reports as STALE, because the check compares it to the gate body
body:
`gate_currency`, `int hooks` and `intent doctor` judge the hook carrier by comparing it against the gate BODY. A correctly installed shim is legitimately a different file from the body it resolves, so a correct install reports as STALE.

FAMILY: one of three where a reporter reads the CARRIER and expects the GATE BODY's properties. Fixing this one does not close the other two -- see the AT-grammar-remedy and gate-not-running issues.

MEASURED, first-hand, as an OPERATOR, before this class had been named -- which is the part worth keeping:

At session pickup on 2026-08-28, `bin/int hooks` in the Intent tree reported the dispatcher STALE and printed its remedy as `intent claude upgrade --apply`. I dry-ran that remedy rather than running it, and measured that it ALSO rewrites `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/settings.json` and the pre-commit chain block -- not only the carrier. I declined to run a canon rewrite in a tree that gates canon currency in order to fix a hook.

THE COST IS NOT THE MESSAGE, IT IS WHAT THE MESSAGE ASKS FOR. A STALE reading that is a property of the mechanism rather than of the install routes the operator to a remedy with a far wider blast radius than the reported defect. The declining was correct only if the STALE was false, which is what this issue says.

Independent measurement (devbin-vc): the shim carries 0 `GUARD_RUNNER` references and 2 `intent/home` references, resolving to `pre-commit.sh`, which carries 47 guard references. The shim is not a degraded body; it is a pointer to one.

FALSIFIER: install the shim carrier in an estate, then run `int hooks`, `gate_currency` and `intent doctor`. If none of them reports that carrier as stale, out-of-date, or behind the template purely on a size or content comparison against the gate body, this is fixed.

SCOPE NOTE: this is an Intent-tree / `int hooks` sighting. It does NOT reproduce in Conflab post-hop, whose doctor reports gate-not-running instead -- a different predicate, filed separately.

SOURCE, CONFIRMED BY READING, NOT BY RUNNING (cited by devbin-vc, re-verified first-hand by intent-dc against the files):

  native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/doctor.rs:1203-1205 -- reads the comparison template as
    home.join("lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit.sh")        <- the GATE BODY

  native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/canon.rs:492-495 -- install_carrier writes
    let shim = template(home, "hooks/pre-commit-shim.sh");
    write_if_changed(&carrier, &shim, applied)?;          <- the SHIM

The file written to the carrier path and the file it is later compared against are different files by construction, so BehindTheTemplate is permanently true on a shim estate.

THE SHARPEST FORM OF THIS IS IN THE CODE'S OWN WORDS. The variant's doc comment at doctor.rs:1065 reads:

  /// Installed, running, and older than the template it was copied from.
  BehindTheTemplate { carrier: usize, template: usize },

"the template it was copied from" is exactly right and exactly what the check does not do: a shim was copied from `pre-commit-shim.sh` and is compared against `pre-commit.sh`. The variant documents the assumption the comparison violates.

`gate_state` is a pure function, so driving every arm is the right closure and would turn "confirmed by reading" into "confirmed by running". That is a build, and it stayed behind the hop window's no-build rule. Stated rather than quietly omitted.
